definitionEn: A structure with walls and a roof, such as a house, school or office.
example: The old building on the corner has been converted into small apartments.

definitionEn: A building where people live, usually intended for one family.
example: Our house has three bedrooms and a small garden at the back.

definitionEn: A separate space inside a building, enclosed by walls and usually a door.
example: Every room in the flat faces south, so it stays bright all day.

definitionEn: A vertical structure that divides or encloses a space in a building.
example: The walls of the living room were painted a soft shade of cream.

definitionEn: The top covering of a building that protects it from rain and weather.
example: Rain leaked through the old roof and stained the bedroom ceiling.

definitionEn: An opening in a wall that lets in light and air, often fitted with glass.
example: Sunlight streamed through the tall window and onto the wooden floor.

definitionEn: A movable barrier that opens and closes an entrance to a building or room.
example: She unlocked the front door and stepped into the quiet hallway.

definitionEn: The level surface inside a building, or one storey of a building.
example: Our office is on the fifth floor of the tall glass building.

definitionEn: A small rectangular block of clay used for building walls.
example: The houses in this street were built with red bricks over a century ago.

definitionEn: A hard, solid piece of rock used as a building material.
example: The cathedral was built from grey stone quarried in the hills nearby.

definitionEn: A structure built over a river, road or valley to allow people to cross.
example: The old stone bridge has carried travellers across the river for centuries.

definitionEn: A tall, narrow building or structure, often standing alone.
example: The clock tower dominates the town square and can be seen for miles.

definitionEn: A large fortified building, usually built in medieval times for defence.
example: Tourists climb the steep path to explore the ruins of the medieval castle.

definitionEn: A building used for Christian worship, often with a tall spire.
example: The little church at the end of the lane has a beautiful wooden roof.

definitionEn: The upper inside surface of a room, opposite the floor.
example: High ceilings and tall windows make the old apartment feel spacious.

definitionEn: A flat piece of clay, stone or ceramic used to cover roofs, floors or walls.
example: The bathroom walls are covered with small blue tiles from Portugal.

definitionEn: To cover a surface with coloured liquid to decorate or protect it.
example: We decided to paint the kitchen walls yellow before moving in.

definitionEn: A set of rooms for living in, on one floor of a larger building.
example: They rent a small flat above the bakery in the town centre.

definitionEn: One level of a building, forming a floor above or below another.
example: The new library will have three storeys with a rooftop reading garden.

definitionEn: An open space enclosed by buildings or walls, usually within a larger complex.
example: Guests gathered in the courtyard, where a fountain splashed beneath orange trees.

definitionEn: A long passage in a building that connects separate rooms.
example: A long corridor with polished wooden doors led to the lecture theatres.

meaningVi: nhà thủy đình, gian triển lãm
definitionEn: A decorative building in a park or garden, or a temporary exhibition structure.
example: The garden pavilion offers shade and a lovely view across the lake.

definitionEn: A small tower projecting from the corner of a larger building, often a castle.
example: A pointed turret rises from each corner of the castle's grey stone walls.

definitionEn: The triangular upper part of a wall at the end of a pitched roof.
example: Carved wooden gables decorate the rooftops of the traditional Dutch houses.

definitionEn: Wood prepared for use in building, such as beams and planks.
example: The barn was constructed from heavy oak timber that has lasted centuries.

definitionEn: A hard building material made from cement mixed with sand, gravel and water.
example: Engineers poured concrete into the moulds to create the bridge's supports.

definitionEn: Glass set into the frames of windows, doors or walls of a building.
example: Floor-to-ceiling glazing fills the living room with natural light.

definitionEn: A low protective wall along the edge of a roof, balcony or bridge.
example: Visitors leaned over the parapet to admire the view of the river below.

definitionEn: The square base on which a column, statue or building rests.
example: The bronze statue stands on a granite plinth in the centre of the square.

definitionEn: A horizontal beam spanning the top of a door or window opening.
example: A carved stone lintel bears the date the house was first built.

definitionEn: One of the sloping beams that support the covering of a roof.
example: Exposed oak rafters give the loft a warm, traditional character.

definitionEn: A flat paved area outside a building, or a row of attached houses.
example: We ate dinner on the terrace overlooking the rooftops of the old town.

definitionEn: A temporary metal framework erected around a building for workers during construction.
example: Scaffolding covered the cathedral's west front while the stonework was repaired.

meaningVi: gờ chỉ trang trí trên tường
definitionEn: A decorative moulding running along the top of a wall or below a ceiling.
example: Elaborate plaster cornices frame the ceilings of the nineteenth-century apartments.

meaningVi: gian nhà, khoảng giữa các cột
definitionEn: A recessed or projecting section of a building between columns, walls or windows.
example: The bay in the library holds a comfortable reading chair beside the window.

definitionEn: A passage inside a house, leading from the front door to other rooms.
example: Coats and umbrellas hung neatly along the hallway by the front door.

definitionEn: An upper space under a roof, often converted into living or working space.
example: They converted the dusty loft into a bright study with skylights.

definitionEn: A small building that guards or controls access through a gate.
example: A gatehouse with a heavy portcullis once guarded the entrance to the fortress.

meaningVi: khu nhà phụ, nhà bổ sung
definitionEn: A smaller building attached to or added onto a larger main building.
example: The museum opened a new annex to display its growing modern art collection.

definitionEn: The arrangement and design of windows and other openings in a building.
example: The fenestration on the north wall was designed to admit soft, even daylight.

definitionEn: Having a roof or ceiling formed by a series of arches.
example: The vaulted ceiling of the nave soars high above the congregation.

definitionEn: A semicircular recess, usually roofed with a half dome, at the end of a church.
example: The apse behind the altar is decorated with gold mosaics of saints.

definitionEn: The central part of a church, extending from the entrance toward the altar.
example: Worshippers filled the nave as the organ music echoed through the vast space.

definitionEn: The transverse arms of a cross-shaped church, crossing the nave.
example: Light poured through the rose window at the end of the transept.

definitionEn: An upper storey with windows that admit light into the central space of a church.
example: Tall clerestory windows flood the nave with light throughout the morning.

definitionEn: A covered walkway around an open courtyard in a monastery or convent.
example: The monks walked slowly around the cloister, reciting prayers in silence.

definitionEn: A horizontal bar across a window or door dividing the opening into sections.
example: A decorative iron transom sits above the carved front door.

definitionEn: A vertical bar dividing a window into separate sections or lights.
example: Stone mullions divide the tall gothic window into elegant narrow panels.

definitionEn: The roughly triangular space between an arch and the surrounding frame or ceiling.
example: Mosaics fill the spandrels beside the arch, depicting scenes from scripture.

definitionEn: A stone at the corner of a building, or a fundamental basis of something.
example: The mayor laid the cornerstone of the new library in a formal ceremony.

definitionEn: An architectural style using raw concrete and bold geometric forms, popular mid-century.
example: Brutalism divides critics, with some admiring its bold concrete forms and others condemning them.

definitionEn: A movement favouring clean lines, function and new materials over traditional ornament.
example: Modernism rejected decorative ornament in favour of honest, functional design.

definitionEn: Relating to a style that playfully mixes historical references with modern forms.
example: The postmodern office block playfully quotes classical columns in bright pastel colours.

definitionEn: Relating to a medieval style with pointed arches and soaring vaulted interiors.
example: Gothic cathedrals feature soaring pointed arches and dramatic stained glass.

definitionEn: Relating to an ornate seventeenth-century style marked by dramatic curves and decoration.
example: The baroque palace is famous for its dramatic curves and gilded ceilings.

definitionEn: Relating to a style that revives classical Greek and Roman forms in later architecture.
example: The neoclassical museum features a grand portico supported by tall white columns.

definitionEn: A porch with a roof supported by columns, forming the entrance to a building.
example: Visitors climb the wide steps to reach the portico of the bank.

definitionEn: A small entrance hall or lobby leading from the outside into a larger building.
example: We waited in the marble vestibule until the guide arrived to greet us.

meaningVi: ban công dài, phòng trưng bày
definitionEn: A long covered passage, or an elevated balcony overlooking a large interior space.
example: The upper gallery overlooks the great hall, where musicians once performed.

definitionEn: A circular building or room, usually topped with a dome.
example: The rotunda's dome is lit by a ring of windows that bathe the floor in light.

definitionEn: The open courtyard enclosed by the outer walls of a medieval castle.
example: Knights trained in the bailey while servants carried water from the well.

definitionEn: The strongest central tower of a medieval castle, used as a last refuge.
example: Defenders retreated to the keep when the outer walls were finally breached.

definitionEn: A deep, water-filled ditch that surrounds a castle as a defence.
example: A drawbridge crossed the moat, which was filled with murky water and reeds.

definitionEn: A high defensive wall with a walkway on top, surrounding a fortified site.
example: Guards patrolled the rampart at night, watching the valley below for intruders.

definitionEn: A notch or opening in a parapet through which soldiers could shoot.
example: Archers aimed through narrow embrasures cut into the fortress walls.

meaningVi: đá nâu, nhà phố đá nâu
definitionEn: A reddish-brown sandstone commonly used for building townhouses in cities.
example: Rows of brownstone townhouses line the quiet, tree-filled street.

definitionEn: Sun-dried clay bricks used as a building material in hot, dry regions.
example: Villagers built their homes from adobe, which keeps interiors cool in the desert heat.

definitionEn: A framework of crossing strips of wood or metal, used as a screen or support.
example: A wooden lattice screen filtered the sunlight across the courtyard floor.

definitionEn: An opening or gap, such as a window, door or vent, that lets in light or air.
example: A small aperture in the dome lets natural light fall onto the altar.

definitionEn: A projecting block of stone or wood that supports a weight such as a beam.
example: Carved stone corbels support the wooden beams of the medieval great hall.

definitionEn: A watertight chamber used to build structures underwater or in soft ground.
example: Workers descended into the caisson to dig the bridge pier beneath the riverbed.

definitionEn: A flat column projecting slightly from a wall, purely decorative or structural.
example: Flat pilasters divide the front wall into sections, framing each of the tall windows.

meaningVi: phần dầm trên cột cổ điển
definitionEn: The horizontal superstructure resting on columns in classical architecture.
example: The entablature above the columns is decorated with carved friezes of athletes.

definitionEn: A horizontal band of sculpture or decoration running along the upper part of a wall.
example: A carved frieze depicting a procession runs around the top of the temple.

definitionEn: A large hall with a roof supported by many columns, common in ancient temples.
example: The hypostyle hall at the temple is filled with hundreds of massive stone columns.

definitionEn: A roof with a double slope on each side, the lower slope steeper than the upper.
example: The mansard roof gave the Parisian apartments an elegant, sloping profile.

definitionEn: A moulding shaped like an S-curve, with concave and convex sections.
example: The arched doorway is framed by an elegant ogee profile carved in pale limestone.

meaningVi: lỗ châu mai trên tường thành
definitionEn: An opening in a castle parapet through which defenders dropped missiles.
example: Defenders dropped stones through the machicolations onto the attacking soldiers below.

definitionEn: A parapet with alternating raised sections and gaps, used on fortified walls.
example: The crenellations along the battlements gave archers cover while they fired.

definitionEn: A fortified outer gateway or watchtower guarding the entrance to a castle.
example: Travellers passed beneath the barbican, where guards checked every cart and rider.

meaningVi: hệ thống sưởi dưới sàn La Mã
definitionEn: An ancient Roman underfloor heating system using hot air channelled beneath the floors.
example: Archaeologists uncovered a hypocaust beneath the villa, its clay pillars still intact.

definitionEn: A glass-enclosed room or terrace designed to collect and enjoy sunlight.
example: A solarium on the top floor floods the flat with warmth throughout winter.

definitionEn: A bay window projecting from an upper storey, supported by brackets or corbels.
example: An oriel window projects over the street, letting the scholar watch passing carriages.

definitionEn: A window set vertically in a sloping roof, projecting from the roof surface.
example: Two dormer windows peer out from the steep slate roof of the cottage.

definitionEn: A cornerstone or external angle of a building, often decorated or emphasised.
example: Rusticated quoins emphasise the corners of the palazzo's rough stone walls.

meaningVi: kỹ thuật đá thô tạo rãnh
definitionEn: Deliberately rough stonework with recessed joints, creating a bold textured effect.
example: The rustication of the lower storey lends the palace a formidable, fortress-like appearance.

definitionEn: Smooth, square-cut stone blocks laid in regular courses to face a wall.
example: The walls are faced with precisely cut ashlar, fitted without visible mortar.

definitionEn: Rough, broken stones or bricks used in building or left after demolition.
example: Rubble masonry filled the core of the wall, faced with dressed stone on each side.

definitionEn: Stonework or brickwork in building, or the craft of working with stone.
example: Skilled masonry work preserved the chapel's walls through five centuries of weather.

definitionEn: A rectangular hole cut into timber to receive a corresponding tenon.
example: The carpenter cut a deep mortise to join the two heavy oak beams securely.

definitionEn: A projecting tongue shaped to fit a mortise, used to join pieces of wood.
example: Each tenon slots precisely into its mortise, requiring no nails or glue.

definitionEn: Skilled woodwork involving the fitting of pieces together without nails.
example: Fine joinery gives the staircase its smooth curves and seamless joints.

definitionEn: A raised framework supporting machinery, cranes or walkways over a site.
example: A steel gantry carried the crane above the construction site all day.

definitionEn: A slender, pointed ornamental turret or peak crowning a Gothic structure.
example: Each pinnacle on the cathedral's roofline is carved with a different saint.

definitionEn: An ornamental top or terminal, often carved, crowning a spire, gable or pinnacle.
example: Bronze finials crown each gable, glinting in the late afternoon sun.

definitionEn: A carved ornament of curling leaves projecting along the edges of Gothic spires.
example: Crockets curl up the sloping edges of the spire, carved in delicate stone foliage.

definitionEn: Decorative stone patterns of intersecting ribs filling the upper part of a Gothic window.
example: The delicate tracery in the window depicts flowers and interlaced geometric shapes.

definitionEn: A four-lobed decorative shape used in tracery, panels and windows.
example: A quatrefoil pattern is carved into the stone parapet above the doorway.

meaningVi: đường giao nhau của hai vòm
definitionEn: The curved line formed where two vaults intersect at right angles.
example: Stone groins bind the ribs together, transferring the weight of the vault downward.

definitionEn: The inner curved surface of an arch or vault, visible from below.
example: Painted decoration covers the intrados of the arch, visible from the nave floor.

definitionEn: The outer curved surface of an arch or vault, facing the outside.
example: Water seeped into cracks along the extrados, weakening the stone arch over time.

meaningVi: viên đá hình nêm của vòm
definitionEn: One of the wedge-shaped stones forming the curve of an arch.
example: Each voussoir was carefully cut to fit precisely into the arch's curve.

definitionEn: The bottom block or course from which an arch springs, resting on a pier or column.
example: The arch springs from a carved impost resting on the slender stone pier.

definitionEn: The flat slab forming the uppermost member of a column's capital.
example: The carved abacus above each column supports the heavy architrave beams.

meaningVi: khung cửa chạm, dầm đỡ cột
definitionEn: The moulded frame surrounding a door or window, or the beam resting on columns.
example: A moulded architrave frames the doorway, drawing the eye toward the carved panel.

definitionEn: A garden structure with columns and cross-beams supporting climbing plants.
example: Wisteria climbs over the wooden pergola, shading the garden seats beneath.

definitionEn: A freestanding, open-sided summerhouse or shelter in a garden or park.
example: We read our books in the white gazebo at the far end of the garden.

definitionEn: A raised structure or room designed to offer an elevated view of the surroundings.
example: From the belvedere on the hilltop, visitors can see the entire valley below.

meaningVi: kim tự tháp bậc thang Lưỡng Hà
definitionEn: A massive stepped tower of ancient Mesopotamia, built of mud brick.
example: The ziggurat rose in tiers above the flat plain of ancient Ur.

definitionEn: A dome-shaped Buddhist monument containing relics or sacred objects.
example: Pilgrims circled the white stupa, spinning prayer wheels as they walked.

definitionEn: A tiered tower with curved eaves, typical of East Asian temples.
example: The five-storey pagoda rises gracefully above the rice fields of the valley.

definitionEn: A tall, slender tower attached to a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.
example: The muezzin climbed the minaret at dawn to call the faithful to prayer.

definitionEn: A sculpted female figure serving as a column supporting an entablature.
example: Six caryatids support the porch of the temple, carved in graceful draped robes.

definitionEn: A sculpted male figure used as a column to support a roof or entablature.
example: Massive telamon figures carry the weight of the balcony on their broad shoulders.

meaningVi: khung trang trí hình bầu dục
definitionEn: An ornamental panel or scroll-shaped frame bearing an inscription or coat of arms.
example: A carved cartouche above the entrance bears the family's coat of arms.

definitionEn: A central column supporting the lintel that divides a doorway into two openings.
example: A sculpted trumeau divides the cathedral portal into two arched doorways.

meaningVi: lộ thiên, không mái ở giữa
definitionEn: Describing a temple that is open to the sky in its centre.
example: The hypaethral temple had an open courtyard that let rain fall into its sanctuary.

definitionEn: An underground chamber or tomb, typically cut into rock.
example: Visitors descend into the hypogeum, a subterranean tomb carved deep beneath the hill.

meaningVi: đài tưởng niệm không có hài cốt
definitionEn: A memorial monument to people buried elsewhere, without actual remains inside.
example: The cenotaph in the square honours soldiers whose bodies were never recovered.

definitionEn: An ancient Egyptian flat-roofed tomb with sloping sides, built of mud brick or stone.
example: The mastaba's sloping walls once concealed the burial chamber of a royal official.
